name: Brandeln
summary: Historic German 3-4 player bidding trick-taking game where soloist bids to win n tricks, lose all, or win all.
rules_text: Play with 28 cards (32-card French pack without 8s). 3 players get 7 cards each; with 4, dealer sits out unless all pass and may play stock. Rank in trump: J > 7 > A > K > Q > 10 > 9; in side suits: A > K > Q > J > 10 > 9 > 7. Bid clockwise starting forehand: Brand is 3 tricks in chosen trump; higher bids 4,5,6 tricks outbid it; Bettel (lose all, no trump) beats 6; Mord (win all 7) is top, Herrenmord is Mord at no trump. Winner announces trump if any and leads. Players must follow suit; if able must head trick in same suit; if void may play any card (early rule required trumping to head). Soloist needs bid tricks, or zero for Bettel, or all for Mord. Scoring: if soloist succeeds each defender pays him game value, if fails he pays each defender. Values e.g. Brand=1-3, Bettel~higher, Mord~highest, Herrenmord double.
rating_reason: Bidding to play solo vs others, Bettel/Mord contracts.
